To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prior knowledge is a significant predictor of learning gains, and the teaching strategies used by students are a significant predictor of SimStudent learning gains, and that SimStudent learning gains are predictive of tutor learning gains.

(1) the prior knowledge is the strongest predictor of post-test scores; and (2) the prior knowledge and teaching strategies (e.g., asking questions, giving explanations, etc.) are predictive of SimStudent’s learning.

(1) students who tutored their synthetic peers better (as measured by their SimStudent’s posttest scores) were more likely to have a more effective tutoring strategy and to use it consistently; (2) the effectiveness of the tutoring strategy was related to the tutor’s prior knowledge; (3) the tutoring strategy was more effective when tutors had a more effective tutoring goal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make SimStudent more effective as a learning tool and how to use SimStudent as a tool to investigate cognitive factors that influence learning.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prior knowledge is the strongest predictor of learning by teaching but the presence of other cognitive factors can have a non-trivial influence.
learning by teaching is a complex process that depends on a number of individual and contextual factors.
the effectiveness of learning by teaching is affected by the prior knowledge and teaching strategies, which are in turn affected by the tutor’s prior knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the learning-by-teaching approach is effective for students with different prior knowledge, but that the effectiveness depends on how the students tutor their peers.
prior knowledge is a necessary but not sufficient condition for learning by teaching.
learning by teaching is an effective learning strategy, especially when students have prior knowledge of the domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learning gains from learning by teaching are affected not only by prior knowledge, but also by the teaching strategy.
learning by teaching is a promising approach to learning, and that it is important to consider both the process and outcome data to understand what makes it effective.
learning by teaching is not a one-size-fits-all approach.
